small_guidance:
- The current kernel re-loads x for every (kh,kw) pair — restructure the inner loop so the IC loop is the outermost reduction and the (kh,kw) gather happens inside, sharing x loads; alternatively try BLOCK_SP=32 with BLOCK_OC=64 to reduce register pressure and enable num_stages=4 pipelining.
- Sweep autotune configs: (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP, BLOCK_IC, num_warps, num_stages) in {(64,32,32,4,3),(128,32,16,8,3),(64,64,16,4,2),(128,64,32,8,2)} — current 128/64/32 produces a [128,256] accumulator which is heavy in registers and may be spilling.
- The pool reduction reshape `tl.sum(v_r, axis=2)` over 4 elements is cheap; instead consider not expanding to POOL*POOL inside the GEMM accumulator — keep BLOCK_SP small (32 pooled = 128 conv outputs) so the dot tile shrinks.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM im2col layout where the GEMM-K axis is `IC*KH*KW` (contiguous loop) and the GEMM-M is OC, GEMM-N is pooled-output-spatial × POOL² conv outputs. With IC=64, KH*KW=9, K=576 fits naturally as 18 iterations of BLOCK_K=32 — only one IC loop instead of nested kh/kw/ic re-gathers, dramatically improving arithmetic intensity.
- Consider a channels-last (NHWC) input layout: permute x once at forward entry so the IC axis is contiguous; this makes the K-direction loads in the GEMM coalesced and lets BLOCK_K=64 work cleanly. Weight can be pre-permuted to (OC, KH, KW, IC) at init.
- Fuse bias + (–sub1) + tanh + (–sub2) + avgpool-2x2 entirely in the epilogue on the accumulator before store (already done) — but compute the pool by allocating the GEMM-N tile as 4× pooled tiles and doing a single in-register 4-way reduction; this halves the output store traffic vs. storing then pooling.
